name: a code span crossing the cut
head: See…
note: A code span the cut opens and does not close counts as crossing the cut, so the cut moves back to before its opening backtick. Cut after `is`, the head would hold the span's opening backtick and no closing one, so that backtick would read as text and the address after it as a live reference.

name: a code span crossing the cut that closes past the window moves the cut back to its backtick

Such a span may close past the window, so it counts as crossing the cut. A copy that read the backtick as text would cut by length and read the address as a live reference.

note: The display tree the page draws (pmdoc, goldmark's link parser) reads [x] as one link whose address runs to the space before the title, its ( unclosed, and [y](... as text of that address, so the reference in it is in [x]'s link. With the ellipsis after it, the address inside the first link's address no longer reads (dispatch://CORE-1))… names nothing), but the key CORE-1 at the same place names the same issue, so the head reads at that place what the text does, and the cut stays: a reference is told apart by what it names, not by how it is written.

The cut falls in that address, so it moves back to the link's [, as it does for the same link without the period. A copy that read the link's address as the parser's whole destination, the period kept, would find no reference there and cut it by length.

A copy that let the backslash take the space would read one link and move the cut back to its [.

name: an address longer than the smallest bound a caller passes keeps its rune cut
head: dispatch://CORE-1/artifact/xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx…
note: 120 is the bound of the dashboard's picker rows (REF_PICKER_TEXT_MAX), the smallest any caller passes. An address can be longer: text.MaxTargetBytes, 2,048 bytes, bounds its target. A bare address has nothing to close, so the cut by length stands, and the ellipsis joins the slug, which then names nothing.

name: an excerpt opening with an address longer than its bound keeps its rune cut
head: dispatch://CORE-1/artifact/xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
note: An excerpt has no ellipsis, so the head reads as an address of an artifact whose slug is the first 213 characters of the text's slug. A bare address has nothing to close, and a head of nothing tells a reader less, so this is the limit the rule states.
